tasks.analysis: Ocean currents are critical components of Earth’s climate system, influencing weather patterns and marine ecosystems. Driven by wind, temperature changes, and differences in salinity, ocean currents distribute heat across the globe. The Gulf Stream, for instance, warms the North Atlantic Current, affecting climate in Europe. Deep ocean currents, known as thermohaline circulation, play a role in regulating global temperatures and carbon dioxide levels.
